correctness.rationale: For PSD matrices D4²=Tr(A^4)+Tr(B^4)-2Tr(ABAB)=||(A-B)(A+B)||_2², giving symmetry, nonnegativity and separation because A²=B² implies A=B for PSD. For fixed trace 2t>0 in Hermitian M2, Pauli A=tI+x·sigma, ||x||<=t gives exact D4²=2||x-y||²(4t²+||x+y||²). For every triple of Bloch vectors, their affine span w+V has dim <=2 with w perpendicular to V; complex coordinate ζ on V maps each point to (sqrt(4t²+4||w||²)*ζ, ζ²) in C², whose ordinary Euclidean distances equal all three d_{4t²} pairwise values; triangle inequality follows for any triple, including PSD boundary. The explicit PSD A=[[2,2],[2,2]], B=diag(2,1), C=diag(2,0) gives independent exact squared distances (240,201,1) with sqrt240>sqrt201+1, and scalar D4(a,b)=|a²-b²| establishes minimal cone-counterexample dimension two. No extension to arbitrary matrix dimension/exponent is asserted.
residual_risks: Only p=4 with common positive trace in M2 is a metric; no arbitrary-size trace-slice theorem or general p>2 result.
A classical metric geometry result for the three-point d_c square-map construction might already be known under a different name; no exhaustive historical-priority certificate.
The Euclidean representation depends on each triple’s affine plane and is not a global embedding for all qubit states.
